opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kenneth Burch (employee ID E007) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E007.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kenneth Burch (E007) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write (admin would require the Payroll Specialist role, which the Analyst role does not own). Requested level is at the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Kenneth Burch (E007) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Kenneth Burch (E007) requested write access to Payroll. HR records show he is a full-time Analyst. For full-time employees, the maximum access is write, and admin would require the Payroll Specialist role (Analyst does not own Payroll). The requested level (write) is at the maximum, so write is granted. (Note: the Security note lists him as a contractor with basic training, which would cap him at read; however, employment type is an HR record, and under the full-time classification the requested write is within policy.)
